entries.title: General is a mounted commander on a white horse
entries.summary: The General’s defining silhouette is a Colonial-era field commander mounted on a white horse, visually distinct from the grounded Commandant.

entries.title: Commandant is grounded, severe, and institutional
entries.summary: The Commandant is an on-foot disciplinarian associated with drill, garrison, fortification, and order rather than heroic mounted command.

entries.title: Leader pairs must contrast in silhouette and mode of power
entries.summary: Each faction’s two Leaders belong together mechanically but must read distinctly in silhouette, setting, dress, props, and temperament.

entries.title: Alchemist is a forbidden natural philosopher, not a cartoon mad scientist
entries.summary: The Alchemist uses an early lab coat/overcoat, tools and loupe, restrained stains, and a meticulous specialist silhouette; he must not look like a butcher.

entries.title: Spirit Walker draws from ritual-performance energy without copying a real performer
entries.summary: The early direction used Maria Franz/Heilung performance energy—layered natural materials, trance, smoke, charms—without copying likeness or making the character specifically Norse. Later Spirit Walker supplements refine the cultural and supernatural direction.

entries.title: Ranger is a frontier scout; Spymaster disappears into society
entries.summary: The Ranger is a practical wilderness/frontier figure, while the Spymaster is a composed urban intelligence operator with social invisibility and secret identity.

entries.title: Banker represents credit; Executive represents operations
entries.summary: The Banker controls debt, credit, and institutional finance, while the Executive is a chartered-company magnate associated with logistics, monopoly, production, and material systems.
